subject: Hosted -> Dedicated transition: pricing offsets and commit structure
messages:
From: Andrew Li <andrew.li@aureliushealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@legalbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing questions for hosted -> dedicated transition

Connor —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're excited about moving some production traffic off the hosted API into a Dedicated pool, but need to understand the economics first. A few specific asks from our side:

- We currently spend roughly $120k/mo on hosted generation (mix of chat + embeddings). What's a reasonable committed pool size (GPUs or vGPU units) to cover our baseline and headroom?
- How do you handle converting our unused hosted credits/commit to Dedicated billing? We're sensitive to double-paying during the transition window.
- Can you outline any \"bridge month\" options if we want a soft migration over 1–3 months?
- What throughput guarantees and SLOs come with the reserved commit vs hosted? We need p95/p99 latency guidance for typical chat workloads.

Also looping in our legal/procurement lead, Priya, for any contract-level notes.

Thanks —
Andrew

Subject: Re: Pricing questions for hosted -> dedicated transition

Andrew —

Appreciate the clear ask. Below is a pragmatic proposal to make migration predictable and to avoid double-billing while preserving throughput guarantees. Attaching a compact tier sheet for reference (Dedicated_Tiers_Aurelius_v3.pdf).

Summary offer (high level):
- Recommended pool sizing (initial): 8 GPU-equivalent units (expected to cover ~80–90% of your baseline; we can scale to 16 if you prefer more headroom).
- Commit term options: 12-mo or 24-mo reserved commits. 12-mo gives baseline 20% device-level discount vs hosted list; 24-mo can get up to 32% depending on commit size.
- Conversion credit mechanics: we will apply a one-time credit equal to the value of your remaining hosted pre-paid credits up to a cap of 6 months of expected Dedicated invoice. Example: if you have $200k in remaining hosted credits, we can apply that $200k as an offset against your first 3–6 monthly Dedicated invoices until exhausted.
- Bridge months: we can structure 0–3 bridge months during which we prorate Dedicated billing and apply hosted credits to offset the Dedicated invoice. During a bridge month we also enable burst capacity to ensure no dropped requests.
- Throughput & SLOs: For an 8-GPU-equivalent pool we guarantee sustained throughput of X tokens/sec for typical chat models (we'll finalize with your evaluation traces). P95 latency target: <= 220 ms; P99 latency SLA: <= 420 ms with automatic routing fallback to hosted if the Dedicated pool is overloaded (subject to agreed fallback budget).

Commercial example (12-mo commit, 8 units):
- Committed monthly invoice: $72,000 (post-discount)
- If you have $120,000 remaining hosted credits, we can apply $72k to month 1 (bridge) and $48k to month 2 as partial offset; remaining $0 thereafter.
- Additionally, we propose a one-time migration credit equal to 8% of the first year's committed spend (applied in month 1) to cover integration/time-to-scale risk.

Next steps I propose: 1) internal sizing call (30m) with your infra/infra-sre team + 2) run a 2-week cross-traffic pilot with production traces so we can validate latency/throughput numbers.

If this looks aligned I can loop in finance for a formal quote and draft LOI for Priya to review.

Cheers —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 13:46:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Pricing questions for hosted -> dedicated transition

Connor —

Saw your draft to Aurelius. A few internal notes before we put a formal quote in HubSpot:

- Migration credit: 8% is reasonable but stretch to 10% only for 24-mo commits or if customer agrees to a 20% minimum uplift in committed throughput (to lock more margin). For 12-mo keep at 6–8%.
- Conversion credit cap: keep the \"up to 6 months\" cap but require the customer to agree to a 30-day notice window before we start consuming hosted credits as offsets. This prevents overlap issues if they re-purchase hosted capacity mid-transition.
- Bridge months: offer 1 guaranteed bridge month included, additional months bill at 50% of committed invoice and consume hosted credits first.
- SLO language: don't promise p99 SLA under heavy burst if fallback to hosted is available. Instead promise p95 SLA at stated latency and p99 best-effort with automatic fallback documented in the rollout annex.

Karthik — can you run a quick margin check on 8 GPU-equivalent at the proposed numbers and confirm finance OK to approve a one-time migration credit at 8% for 12-mo deals? If not, we'll push for 12-mo at 6% and 24-mo at 10%.

-Marissa

Marissa / Connor —

Quick finance read: at $72k/mo committed for 12 months (8-unit example) the contribution margin after estimated infra + ops is ~28% at our current cost model — acceptable for a strategic account. Approving a one-time migration credit of 8% of first-year committed spend is within guidelines for ARR > $500k. If they push for 10% we should require a 24-mo commit or a 20% increase in baseline commit.

I approve the following commercial guardrails:
- 12-mo: migration credit 6–8% (default 8% if signed within 14 days of quote).
- 24-mo: migration credit up to 10% and an additional 5% off invoice (total incremental discount capped at 32%).
- Bridge months: 1 free (hosted credits first), additional months at 50% invoice with continued credit application.

I'll drop the approved pricing into HubSpot and flag the deal for legal review re: SLA language.

-Karthik

Connor, Marissa, Karthik —

Thanks for the quick follow-ups and for tightening the commercial guardrails. The structure looks sensible; a few contractual asks from our side before we sign:

1) Throughput guarantee: we need a firm p99 latency SLA of <= 350 ms for standard chat workload (this is a hard requirement tied to our user SLAs). If that is not feasible, we need a clearly defined credit formula when SLA is missed.
2) Conversion credit wording: we need the applied credit to be visible on the invoice as a line item and a clear burn schedule (month-by-month) so our finance team can reconcile.
3) Bridge month scheduling: we'll take 2 bridge months, but need the ability to opt-out of month 2 if performance is acceptable.

If you can get the above into an LOI (Priya is ready to review legal language) we'll target an internal sign on Nov 18 and plan the sizing call next week. Also please add a DocuSign LOI and the HubSpot quote link in your next note.

I'll stand by for your revised LOI.

—Andrew
